blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you, my Lord. [Mother of Babies E & F], please.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: For the jury, my Lord -- I know you reminded the jury on Friday -- we are of course moving on to count 5.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: [MOTHER OF BABIES E & F] (sworn)
Examination-in-chief by MR JOHNSON

Thank you. It's quite a big room and you have quite a soft voice, so if you wouldn't mind, please, it's a slightly artificial exercise, but the questions, generally speaking, come from this direction. If you could try to give your answers to the jury. And it may help you if you look at the jury when you speak, if you don't mind. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: So imagining that you're shouting at your kids, can you tell the jury what your name is, please?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: [Mother of Babies E & F].
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: [Mother of Babies E & F], on 29 July 2015 did you give birth to identical twin sons, [Baby E] and [Baby F]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Was that at the Countess of Chester Hospital?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: As a matter of fact, and I'm not asking you to tell us your address, but did you live in that general area?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Where had you expected to be giving birth?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: The Liverpool Women's Hospital.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: But for capacity reasons, were you taken to Chester?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can you remember now how far your pregnancy was advanced when you gave birth on 29 July?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: 29 weeks and 5 days.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: When you gave birth, what was the impression that you had of the state of health of your twin sons?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I thought they were in good condition for the gestation.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Was [Baby E] born first?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And followed, about a minute later, by [Baby F]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: How long was it before you had physical contact with your boys after giving birth?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I got to go to the neonatal unit at around 11.20 in the evening, after having them just before 6 o'clock in the evening.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Were you able, given your condition and their condition, to spend a lot of time with them at that stage?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No. Just a few minutes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So that was 29 July, which was a Wednesday. Did you stay in hospital yourself for quite a period of time after they, the lads, had been born?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The following day, Thursday, 30 July, were you able to visit the boys?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And how far away from the neonatal unit were you being accommodated?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I was upstairs in the post-natal ward. I'm unsure of how far away that is, but it was in a lift.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. Perhaps in time, how long, generally speaking, would it take you to get from the post-natal ward down or along or up to the neonatal ward?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I had had a section, so it took me probably a little bit longer than what it would probably take normally, so probably about 5, 10 minutes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Were you able to cuddle your boys on 30 July?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: [Baby E].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: [Baby E]. Was there any reason why you were able to cuddle [Baby E] and not cuddle [Baby F]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: [Baby E] wasn't on his CPAP, so he didn't have all the wires that [Baby F] did.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Sorry, just pause for a moment. I know it is very difficult. You do have a soft voice. As Mr Johnson has said, this is a large room. If you could face towards the jury.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Sorry.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: No, don't worry at all. The loop isn't working apparently.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (Pause)
Thank you, Mr Murphy.
There's interference coming through on the loop, I'm told, my Lord, I don't know why that is. Normally it's all right as long as the voices are loud enough, so that would help.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I think we're going to have to abandon the loop for the moment. So that means you've got to speak even louder, [Mother of Babies E & F], I'm sorry. As Mr Johnson said, imagine you're speaking to the people at the back of the jury. If you think that then you will raise your voice.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Okay.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I'm just asking Ms Letby to make sure she can tell us if she can't hear. It's difficult behind the glass.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: If you can't hear, just raise a hand because I'll see that. All right?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Okay. You're not the first and you won't be the last. All right?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: I say it to nearly every witness to comes into court wherever I am, so don't feel embarrassed or different in any way. It's natural and you're quietly spoken. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Do you go to the match?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Never mind, okay.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Now, 30 July, which was the Thursday, so the lads' first full day, so to speak. Had you made a decision about how you wanted your sons to be fed?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And what was your decision, please?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I wanted them to have my breast milk.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What steps had you decided to take in order for them to get what you wanted them to get in terms of their feed?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Were you providing breast milk yourself?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And were you helped by the nurses to express that so that it could be provided to them?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Whilst that regime was establishing itself, had you agreed for them to have donor milk?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: But in due course, did you manage to establish a regime whereby you were able to provide your own milk for the lads?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes. That was very important to me.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: On 31 July, which was the Friday, did you produce milk for your sons and drop it off at the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: As you were thinking then, how did providing your milk for your sons feature in a list of important things for you to do?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: It was the only thing I could do for them at that point.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I had to do it. It was non-negotiable for me.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. Were you getting help and support from the nursing staff to achieve what it was you were seeking to achieve?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So taking those 2 days then, that is Thursday the 30th and Friday, 31 July, in general terms how were the lads progressing?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Really well.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: As it appeared to you, on just those 2 days, who was doing the better of [Baby E] and [Baby F]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Sorry?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Which of the lads was doing better at that stage?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Oh, [Baby E].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: By Saturday, 1 August, how were the boys progressing?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Really well.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You were a distance from home in Chester?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Were you keen to get back home or closer to home at least?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Absolutely.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What were you waiting for so far as getting back towards home was concerned?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Transport to be able to take both boys, so rather than being able to transport one baby, we needed two ambulances to take them and for those to be available for neonatal babies.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: As you understood it, was there any -- other than physically getting two ambulances with the required facilities to carry out the transfer, so far as the health of the lads was concerned, did you understand that there was anything blocking them moving other than just getting the transport?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No. We were informed by staff on the unit that -- we actually asked if we would like to move closer to home, to our local hospital, so at that point I was under the impression that both my boys were well enough to travel.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Had you had any -- by 1 August, which was the Sunday, sorry, the Saturday, I beg your pardon, had you had skin-to-skin contact with them?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And how were your sons managing in terms of the skinto-skin contact?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: They were managing fine. We were never informed that there was anything to say that they weren't managing fine.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So that's 1 August, the Saturday. Moving on to 2 August, the Sunday, were you still waiting for transport?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Were the boys always in their incubators on the Sunday or were they coming out of the incubators?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Um... From memory, I think -- well, yeah, they were out of the incubators. Yes, they were out of the incubators, both of them.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Just concentrating on [Baby E] first for a second, how was he breathing out of the incubator?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Beautifully.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And [Baby F]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Great.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Sorry, you dropped your voice there.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Sorry. Great.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Was there -- do you remember an occasion when you were told that there was a potential issue over the production of insulin, the blood sugars, of the boys?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I don't remember a specific conversation, but I do recall that being mentioned, that neonatal babies struggle to maintain levels of insulin, that was totally normal.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: 3 August. How were the boys doing by Monday, 3 August?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Great. They were doing really well. [Baby F] had come off his CPAP and gone on to Optiflow and we were absolutely thrilled that both boys were doing so well and, yeah, we couldn't have asked for any more than that. They were both progressing.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What about [Baby E]? How was he doing on Monday the 3rd during the day?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: [Baby E] was always thriving.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You've already told us that you were an inpatient yourself at the Countess. Was your husband staying over or was he commuting to and from the hospital?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No, he was commuting to and from the hospital.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And without giving away too much detail, geographically was your home at the time in effect on the other side of Liverpool from Chester?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Over an hour.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Over an hour away, okay.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did there come a stage on Monday when your husband, [Father of Babies E & F], went home?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did he have any -- as far as you were concerned, had he gone home for a specific reason, to do anything in anticipation of anything?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes, he'd gone home to prepare the house because he'd been there for a while I was in hospital and he was going home to tidy up and get prepared for me coming home because we believed that that was imminent, that the boys were getting transferred to a local hospital, which would mean I would be sleeping at home.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can you remember approximately the time of the day on Monday the 3rd when your husband [Father of Babies E & F] left the hospital to go home?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes, it was about 5 o'clock.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that in the afternoon?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: In the afternoon.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can you remember what you were doing when [Father of Babies E & F] left you in hospital?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I was having skin-to-skin with [Baby E].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can you remember the time when your direct contact with [Baby E] ended on Monday, 3 August?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: So you mean that skin-to-skin contact?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. What time did that finish?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: About 6.30-ish.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did you do anything else for your son before you left him in the care of the nursing staff?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes. I changed his nappy and done all his -- what they call cares, so that was cleaning him, cleaning under his neck, cleaning his eyes and things like that.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What sort of state were you in by this stage, by the 3rd? Did you feel you'd fully recovered or were you still tired?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I was still sensitive and sore and fragile, but I was just over the moon, I was absolutely over the moon. My two boys were perfect.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And were you still managing to provide milk for them to be fed?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So you left the lads in the neonatal unit and where did you go from the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I went up to the post-natal ward.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What did you need to do when you got to the post-natal ward?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Express milk and have something to eat.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can you remember roughly what time it was that you carried out those two tasks?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: It would have been between 7 and about 8.30. I can't give an exact...
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No. I don't think anyone would expect you to be exact, but that's the time as you remember it.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Now having expressed the milk for your sons, and having had your own food, what did you decide to do?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: What I did every time: every time I expressed milk I took it straight down to the neonatal unit, even if it was in the night. So every 2 to 3 hours I would express and I would take it to the unit.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What time was it when you arrived at the unit with the milk?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: A touch before 9 o'clock.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I just want to deal with the layout in the unit, all right? I think you drew a plan for the police. Do you remember
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: drawing that plan? By your facial expression, you don't look too impressed with your own plan.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: It wasn't my finest hour.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm sure we all understand. I wonder whether we could see the plan on the screen, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This is one of the plans. I'm not going to comment on how good, bad or indifferent it is, but for the sake of the record it's J2424.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that all written by you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: The bit down the side.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So the bit down the right-hand side is written by you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No, it's not written by me. And this (indicating), that isn't written by me.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So are those the bits that aren't written by you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: (Inaudible).
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And the bit along the top, "high dependency children"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Do you know whose writing that is?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I think that's my family liaison (inaudible), I'm unsure.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You're just going to have to keep your voice up a bit.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I think that's the family liaison's writing.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So the police officer that was speaking to you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay. Were you describing what --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I struggled.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I'm not very visual with things like that, so I can see it in my own mind, but I couldn't put it on -- I physically
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: couldn't put it on to the paper and he was just telling me to do my best and then he added some of the writing in.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay. As you were describing it?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: As I described it, at my request.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay. So you were directing what was written and where it was written?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay, I understand.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, we can see just at the top where it says "high dependency children", there is what looks like a pretty much a square box and within the square box are two rectangular boxes. One has the name [Baby E] and the other has [Baby F] against it. If we enlarge that a bit more, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think what it says is, turning sideways, "room 1" and then two rectangles, one having [Baby F] against it and one having [Baby E] against it. Is that right?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that how you remembered it?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay. So the lads were together in a room. The room, as you remember it, was room number 1; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Were they both in incubators --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: They were.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: -- on 3 August? Can you remember now whether there were any other children in the room, any other babies in the room?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I don't think there was, but I can't remember.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay. Let's go back to that night then, please. If we could just remove that from the screen. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You had gone down with the purpose of delivering the milk for the boys. Did you go into room number 1?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Other than your children, was anyone else in room number 1?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Who else was in room number 1?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Lucy Letby.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Right. Were any other adults in the room?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What could you see or hear when you walked into the room?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I could hear my son crying and it was like nothing I'd heard before. I walked over to the incubator to see he had blood coming out of his mouth and I panicked.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I was panicking because I felt like there was something wrong.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay. I just want to get a bit more detail from you, all right? We all realise it's very difficult for you to give this detail, but, first of all, which of your sons are you talking about?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: [Baby E].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Was Lucy Letby near [Baby E] when you walked in?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No, she was -- in between [Baby E]'s incubator, there was a workstation and she was at the workstation at the side of -- yes, she was at the workstation.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay. I'll just try and help you with -- what I'll show you, if Mr Murphy can help me, is a video of the room.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Are you all right watching that?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: (Witness nods).
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: There are no children in the room, okay? I don't know whether Mr Murphy, you could help by locating the video for me. This is the shakier of the videos, if I can put it that way.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: If you need to watch this more than once, [Mother of Babies E & F], you tell us, all right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Okay.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: (Video played to the court)
Can we just stop it there, please.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What we've just seen there, [Mother of Babies E & F], is two separate entrances into the same room. The room is partially divided by a wall, which is the wall we can see to the right of the screen at the moment, which is between the two doors. Okay?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: We can see the positions of four incubators within the room. Looking at the video, can you remember which of those incubators your sons were in?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Which of the incubators?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: The ones immediately...
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: On the other side from the wall we're looking at now?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you, Mr Murphy. So that's, just for the record, at 01:09 on that video.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: The workstation that you were speaking of where Lucy Letby was, where is that -- is that shown on the video?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: It was round -- she was round here (indicating).
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So you're indicating to the right-hand side of the screen as we're looking at that still there?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay. Was Lucy Letby sitting or standing?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No, standing.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: She was standing. And just to help us, which of the two incubators was which of your lads in?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: [Baby E] and [Baby F].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: [Baby E] in the one to the right as we're looking at the picture and [Baby F] up towards the left of the picture.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did you come through the door that the camera operator is standing in as we look at that still?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Rather than nodding your head, would you mind --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Sorry, yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Lots of witnesses do it, all right, just nod, but if you wouldn't mind verbalising the answer. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Just describe again for us what you could hear, please, [Mother of Babies E & F].
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Crying, like...
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What sort of a cry?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: It was a sound that shouldn't have come from a tiny baby. I can't explain what that sound was. It was...
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It was horrendous. More of a scream than a cry.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And how long before you walked into the room could you hear that; can you remember?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I could hear it in the little corridor.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: The main corridor.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: We can't actually see the door. Through that door where the cameraman is?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes. There's the door. Thank you, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that what you mean, [Mother of Babies E & F]?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: So as we know from the corridor, that's the right-hand door if you're in the corridor.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, thank you, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: And just to be entirely clear, what was Lucy Letby doing as you walked in, hearing what you could hear?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: She was busy doing something, but she wasn't near [Baby E].
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: What did you do?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I immediately went to [Baby E] and -- because when the boys were born, we were told to use a containment technique, which is putting your hand on the baby's head and on the tummy to make them feel like they're still in your tummy.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: So I tried doing that. That's meant to make them feel calm and comforted. I tried doing that and it didn't work.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So did [Baby E] continue to make the same noise?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Doing your best, how long did he continue to make that noise?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: He was still making that when I left.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Let's just try and define the period that you were there from arriving to leaving and then we'll fill in what happened during that time. Approximately how long were you in the unit in that room with your lads?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: About 10 minutes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Right. When you did this containment technique with [Baby E] with your hands, was there anything unusual that you could see on or about [Baby E]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes, there was blood on his face, round his mouth.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can you remember now, were you asked by the police to draw on a pre-drawn picture of a baby's face --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: -- to indicate where the blood was?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: If we could go to that, please, Mr Murphy. It's page 27 of the bundle I gave you.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This, my Lord, for the record is CLG/9, which is J2434.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is this the diagram that you annotated, [Mother of Babies E & F]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm sure it's perfectly obvious to everybody, but can you just describe the alteration that you have made to the plan?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Round the mouth.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So describing it in a rather inelegant way, it's almost like a goatee beard?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Sorry, for the sake of clarity -- it's difficult to see -- was it above the top lip?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Not really. A little bit, but not as much as on the bottom.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: That's better, yes, thank you, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: So you've shaded in, almost like a pencil moustache -- that's the way it looks -- and below the bottom lip and just above the point of the chin, that area between, you have put shading; is that right?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay. What you saw was blood; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did you ask Lucy Letby about what it was you could see?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What did you say to her?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I asked why he was bleeding and what was wrong.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did she give you a response?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What did she say?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: She said the feed tube from the back of his throat will have been rubbing and that will have caused the blood.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did you accept that explanation?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Were you concerned about the explanation?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did Lucy Letby say anything else to you?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: She told me to go back to the ward.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did you do what you were told by her?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Why did you do what you were told by her?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Because she was in authority and she knew better than me and I trusted her completely.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did she say what she would do about the problem?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: She said the registrar was on his way and if there was a problem, someone would ring up to the post-natal ward.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And did you accept that explanation?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did you return to the post-natal ward?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did you do anything when you got back to the post-natal ward?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I rung my husband.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Any particular reason why you rang your husband?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I knew there was something very wrong. I was frightened. I didn't take my phone downstairs and I needed to speak to him, I needed to tell him.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay. Let's deal with -- did there come a stage much later in the process when you were trying to put together the sequence of events?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And when you were doing that, did you remember going back to the -- do you remember what you have just told us, that you went back to the post-natal ward and you made this telephone call?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: All right. Did you get a printed version of your telephone records?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I did.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And did you identify from the telephone records the call that you made when you returned to the post-natal ward?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I did.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: With the help of Mr Murphy again, please, it's page 8 of the documents -- this, for the jury's information, will appear in the sequence of events as well when we go through the sequence. It's J2431.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: This is an edited version of your phone records, [Mother of Babies E & F], okay? So we're not telling the world at large what people's telephone numbers are or were at the time.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that your writing on the telephone record?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I can read it perfectly well, but just for the sake of the record, is there a number 1 at the top, which has been partially obscured by the way the document has been copied?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And have you written on it:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "When I called [Father of Babies E & F] to tell him there was something wrong"?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay. Is there then a number 1 to the right of that manuscript?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Then an asterisk, a star?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What's the time of the call to [Father of Babies E & F] to tell him there was something wrong?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: 21.11.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So if we highlight that. Can we see that that was a call that lasted 4 minutes and 25 seconds?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And that number ending, is it 5808 or 5800?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: 5800.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: 5800 was [Father of Babies E & F]'s number at the time?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did you speak to your husband about your concerns?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I did.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Having spoken to him, did you remain on the post-natal ward?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: When did you next return to the neonatal ward?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: It was later on that evening, it would have been...
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It may be fairer to you if you just tell us in summary form what was going on the next time you went to the neonatal ward. What was happening in the neonatal ward?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I was sat in the corridor, actually inside the neonatal unit, and I was watching a team of people around [Baby E]'s incubator, working on him.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So this was [Baby E] being resuscitated the next time you went? Okay. We have a time for that, all right? So I won't ask you about that. But I just want to make sure we've filled in the time between you going back to the post-natal ward and you going down when [Baby E] was being resuscitated.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Okay.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So just trying to put yourself back into that time for us, please, [Mother of Babies E & F], in that intervening time what were you doing?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Panicking. I'd had conversations with the midwife, who had come to administer medication to me. A lot of that time was panicking and waiting and waiting because I was following the rules. I was told that if there was a problem, I'd be told to go.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Who had told you what the rules were so far as this period of time was concerned?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Well, the rules were: go back upstairs and if there's a problem I'll call you. And that was Lucy Letby on the neonatal unit and I followed those rules.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. Can you remember how you were called back to the unit, who was responsible for calling you back? How did you get a message?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: The midwife came and spoke to me and asked me to call my husband and she spoke to him on the phone.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay. Can we see that call on this telephone record, [Mother of Babies E & F]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: What time is it shown as on the telephone record?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: 22.52.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So that's number 2; is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: You have written:
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: "Midwife rung [Father of Babies E & F] to tell him to come into the hospital after neonatal rung the maternity ward."
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is that right?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Is there any reason why it was the midwife who spoke to [Father of Babies E & F] rather than you speaking to [Father of Babies E & F]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I have no idea. I'm presuming because I wasn't...
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I was very upset and... I... I knew there was something wrong and I'd known from leaving him, but I left.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Sorry.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, no, don't be sorry. It's quite all right.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't want to make things unnecessarily difficult for you, all right, because there are many doctors and medical professionals who can give us the details about what happened with [Baby E] when he was being resuscitated. But does it come to this, that you were taken back down to the neonatal unit later on?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: To use your words, or an approximation of your words, the medical team were working on [Baby E]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And ultimately, their best efforts were unsuccessful?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: We'll leave it at that with you because others are in a less sensitive position than you to explain what happened there.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: But I just want to deal with what happened afterwards, please, once [Baby E] had passed away.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Okay.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did you have any contact with Lucy Letby at that stage?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can you tell us what happened in relation to that contact with Lucy Letby after the death of [Baby E]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I was asked if I would like to bath [Baby E] and at that moment I didn't feel I was able to. I was... I was just broken and I couldn't. So Lucy Letby bathed him in front of me in the neonatal unit. After he was bathed, he was placed in a white gown and I just remember being thankful because we had no clothes for him because he was so little.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: (Pause)
And he was given back to us and then went in his incubator. And that's where he stayed.
Did one of the doctors have a conversation with you and your husband about the issue of a post-mortem examination of [Baby E]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes. We were asked about a post-mortem and I think my husband asked some questions and I think those questions were along the lines of: what will a post-mortem tell us? And she told us that it wouldn't tell us very much and it wouldn't be able to tell us any more than what she was telling us of how he died. She spoke about it would delay -- it would... It would delay our transfer back home, it would mean if we got transferred back home, we would be leaving [Baby E], and we just wanted to take him home.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did there come a stage when you were given anything by Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes, we were given a memory box, which totally surprised me because at that moment I hadn't even thought -well, I... It was just all his things, footprints, there was a little memory card with pictures on, a lock of his hair, a candle, a teddy, and I just -- I was just so over, overcome with emotion that this had been provided for me because I had no other memories apart from that.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did you ever get a -- you have told us about a teddy for [Baby E]. Did you ever get another teddy?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes, we got a matching one for [Baby F], actually those teddies were swapped over, so [Baby E] got [Baby F]'s teddy and [Baby F] got [Baby E]'s teddy.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: In relation to [Baby F] and his teddy, did you ever get anything else from Lucy Letby?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: There was a picture, not long... I think it was a few days after. I'm struggling to recall the actual date.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Don't worry about the precise date, but approximately was this whilst [Baby F] was still in the Countess of Chester Hospital?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: [Baby F] was in the Countess of Chester Hospital and we had been to visit [Baby E] at the chapel of rest. Until his funeral, we made the journey home every day until it was his funeral, and when we come back one day there was a picture, she'd presented me with a picture of [Baby F] holding his -- we called it his [Baby E] bear, and she said, "I got this picture, he rolled over and hugged his [Baby E] bear and I thought it was so amazing, so I took a picture for you".
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So she was suggesting to you that [Baby F] had rolled over and cuddled the bear?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did there come a time when you sent a card to the staff on the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Was that done through one of these Internet companies where you can, in effect, build your own card?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And I think Moonpig is one.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I'm sure other card services are available. Is it that sort of a card that we're talking about?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Did that card on its front have a picture of your boys?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Just...
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Just [Baby F]?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: And within it, did it express your -- you, your husband [Father of Babies E & F] and [Baby F]'s -- thanks to the staff on the neonatal unit?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I want to ask you one other point, please, [Mother of Babies E & F]. On the question of your son [Baby F]. Has he ever had any -- how old is he now?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Seven.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Has he ever had any unusual bleeding issues in the 7 years that you've had him?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you, [Mother of Babies E & F].
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: My Lord, those are all the questions I have at this stage.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Do you know about how long you're likely to be?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Probably about half an hour to 45 minutes, something like that, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Right.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We have got into the habit of having a break during the course of the morning, some time usually around 11.45 to 12.00. We could either have a break now or we could continue and possibly have a break before you finish your evidence or possibly even get to the end of your evidence. Would you like to continue all the way through now?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: It's up to you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: It is not up to me, it's up to you. What would you like? Should we see how you get on maybe have a break in around half an hour?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: All right.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Cross-examination by MR MYERS

[Mother of Babies E & F], if at any point you need to stop, as his Lordship says, you must say so. Can I say before I ask my questions, everybody will understand what an awful experience you have had and your husband. I have to ask you questions about it, but I really want to emphasise, nothing I say is meant to be insensitive. I'll be as quick as I can be. I make it plain that whatever I'm asking and whatever happened, nobody suggests that you haven't done everything you could do. You said about you'd left him and whatever, but you did all that
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: you could do, so nothing I say is meant to suggest anything other than that. All right?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: There will be some things that I ask that you may disagree with and if that happens, could I ask you to say that you disagree or you don't accept what I say and then I can put those things to you and you can make that plain and then we can move on to the next thing.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Okay.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Is that all right?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: All right.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Just for a little background for us, was this, so we can follow, your first babies, this was the first time you'd been in hospital as a new mum?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'm going to ask you to keep your voice up if you could, please.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So had you spent much time -- I don't want to ask any personal details, but had you spent much time in hospitals before this in any capacity with babies, anything like that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: When you came to help the police with this, you made -the first statement you made was in July 2017. You made a few other ones afterwards, but July 2017. Did you make some notes shortly after that just to help your memory?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So you'd be able to tell the police?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Were those notes also notes that you made in July 2017 or in 2017?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Again, so you were thinking back to things that had happened back in June and August 2015?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: End of July and August?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I think you misspoke, you said June and August.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I apologise.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: The end of July and beginning of August.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: So almost exactly 2 years.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I'm going to go through some of the details and some of the timings. I'll ask you generally now, you can agree or disagree, but do you think it's possible that any of the timings you've got could be not accurate, the timings you have given us?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: In respect of what timings?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: When you say for instance you went down at 9 o'clock or about 9 o'clock, is that a timing you're quite clear about?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Or is that approximate?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We'll go through it and have a look. What happened that night, perhaps we can agree about this, must have been very intense and very upsetting.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: And so what I'd like to look at is whether there's any areas where any of the detail that you've got could at all be mixed with any other detail or any other timing as we go along. That's what I'm looking at.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Okay.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You will tell me if you disagree.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Okay.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So that you know where I'm coming from with the questions and so that everybody knows, so you know what lies behind them,
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: can I suggest to you that there were three times you went down that evening. I'm going to suggest it and then we'll go over it and you tell me if this is right or wrong. Is that okay?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I am doing to so you know where I am coming from because I don't want it to suddenly come as a surprise what I'm suggesting.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'm going to suggest to you that you'd gone down round about 8 o'clock, which is the handover time on the unit --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Right.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: -- and you were doing cares, certainly with [Baby E], round about then. Let me suggest this and we'll go over it.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Then I'm going to suggest that actually it's nearer to 10 o'clock than 9 o'clock that you went down with the breast milk.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: And then you went back again when [Baby E] was being resuscitated round about 11 o'clock. So I know you have said you went down at 9 and then you went back later, and what I'm asking you to consider is whether you'd gone down at 8 and then 10 and then later.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No, that's not the case.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You disagree with that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Absolutely.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'm suggesting that, you disagree with it.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes, okay.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'll come back to some more detail, but I'm going to go through the things now that you've been talking about.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Okay.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Let's just go through what you describe when you say you went down at 9 o'clock. I'm going to ask you about that next.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You told us there were two things about [Baby E] at that time or two in particular. One was how upset he was. That's one of them, isn't it? And the other was that there was blood coming out of his mouth; is that right?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: (Witness nods).
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You're nodding, it's tempting to nod.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I'm sorry, yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: About the upset first of all, let me ask you about the crying. When you went down, [Mother of Babies E & F], to the unit that evening, there were other staff, other nurses, in the unit, weren't there?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I would imagine so, but I didn't come into contact with anybody.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You've described it as "very loud" and you said "horrendous screaming and crying".
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes. Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: On your account, at no time did any other nurse come into the nursery, did she or he?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No, not that I'm aware of.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'm not going to disagree that [Baby E] was upset when you went down. What I'm looking at is just how upset he was, right? And what I'm going to suggest to you is that he wasn't as upset to the degree that you describe. It wasn't as bad as that. Because you said it was horrendous.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: It was horrendous.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'm respectfully disagreeing and saying he was upset, but it wasn't as horrendous as you're saying. In your mind you say it was horrendous.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Okay.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'm going to ask you a little bit about the blood. I'll be as quick as I can with this. You said to start with that there was blood coming out of his mouth and you drew a picture, didn't you? Did the blood go anywhere else apart from on his chin?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: It was on his -- a little bit.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: A little bit on the lip?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: And underneath.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Just so we can be quite clear, you're not describing something where there is blood coming out and it's going on his clothes or over the bedding or anything like that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It's that you could see certainly what looked like blood, you would say it was blood, but you could see it round about his chin in that area like we saw on that picture?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You say on clothes. Perhaps we could have some evidence of what clothing --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: He wasn't wearing any clothing.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: But on your clothes, for instance, because you contained him, didn't you?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I had my hand on the top of his head and on his stomach.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: But to be quite clear, and this is the point I am asking and I think you agree, you're not describing it coming out and going over things like that --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: -- or on the bedding or anything like that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: One of the descriptions that you gave to the police later, [Mother of Babies E & F], was this, and just see if you agree, you said:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "It was around his bottom chin and the bottom lip [like on the picture you've drawn]. It wasn't thick, it's difficult to explain what it was like, it was like a dribble pattern on his skin. It wasn't completely fresh."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Does that sort of describe what it was that you saw?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: (Witness nods). Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: All right. I know you said it's blood and that's how you say -- that's what you say you saw. I'll ask in case it makes any difference: is it possible that what you saw was some sort of dark liquid with flecks of blood in it around his chin?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: It was blood.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's right, you say it was blood. All right. I'm suggesting if you did see anything like that at that time it might have been what's called a dark aspirate with flecks of material in it, but you say it was blood.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: It was blood.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: All right. And it struck you as not completely fresh?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Again, just going through some of the details that you have given us, [Mother of Babies E & F], you mentioned that after you'd been downstairs, you went upstairs and you saw -did you see -- was it the midwife?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: A midwife come in.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Is that the midwife who had been looking after you generally?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: That evening, yes. There was different midwives on.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: There was a lot of different midwives.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Had you seen this one before?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No, it was the first time I'd come into contact with this one.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Did you speak to her about what had happened?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes, I was distraught.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'm not going to suggest you weren't anxious and you weren't upset.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Mm-hm.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I am going to suggest, and you can disagree with it if you want to, [Mother of Babies E & F], that actually at this time you were worried, but it was much later in the evening that you became distraught.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes, okay.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Do you agree or disagree with that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I disagree. I was...
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You say you were distraught here?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes, I knew there was something very wrong.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: All right. I'm just showing where the differences are, but trying to get on with it quickly so we don't spend too long with it.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Was the midwife called Susan?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Susan Brooks?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I don't know her last name.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We'll see sooner or later, I imagine, a note from Susan Brooks, who describes how she had been told by you that, it must be [Baby E], had deteriorated slightly.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Okay.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: This is the note. We'll come to the note later in the evidence.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Okay.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'm going to suggest that at that point we have that because you weren't saying at that point that you were -something was very wrong, you might have said you were anxious but you weren't actually saying anything was very wrong.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I said that to my husband on the phone, I told him there was something very wrong.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Right. I'm going to suggest you didn't say that to the midwife even though you were talking with her, did you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I can't remember that full conversation, but I was very upset.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Right. All right. I've explained where I'm coming from and you're making it clear where you come from, so I'll move on with the next detail.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: With your husband, we know there was a phone call at 21.11. We've seen that on the records. Then there was a later call, wasn't there, at about 22.42?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Again, not disputing you were anxious about things that were taking place at the very least. You say you were more than anxious, you say you were very worried?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'm not going to dispute that you mentioned that you had seen what you thought was blood on [Baby E]. I'm not disputing that. But did you speak to your husband -- when you spoke to him later, at 22.52, did you tell him then as well, or at all, that there was a lot of blood coming from [Baby E] at that time?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I don't remember a conversation with [Father of Babies E & F] at that point.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It was Sue, the nurse, who was having a conversation with [Father of Babies E & F].
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You checked your phone records some time after the night that this all happened, didn't you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: There was an issue with the hospital, wasn't there, about timings --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: -- incidentally and you'd wanted just to have a look at the timings, hadn't you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Again, I'm just asking and I give you the opportunity to respond to this, whether actually at the phone call at 9.11, whilst you were anxious, you weren't as worried as you were later on, when you'd been called down for the resuscitation. Is it possible that, looking back, you've kind of transferred some of the very big worry you had later to that phone call at 9.11? Is that possible, do you think?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No, it's not possible.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I suggest it is, but you disagree with me about that.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes, I disagree.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's why I'm doing it this way so we can make it quite clear. All right.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Can I go through then some suggestions I'm going to make to you about what happened. Exactly the same: you're absolutely free to agree or disagree as you like, [Mother of Babies E & F].
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Okay.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I've asked you whether you went down to do cares at 8 o'clock and you say that --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You didn't, all right. I've suggested to you that the time you did go down with the breast milk is later than 9, it might even be as late as 10, but you disagree with that.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I disagree.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: All right. I suggest to you that there was no time that Ms Letby said the tube was irritating [Baby E].
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That isn't something that she said.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I disagree.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Okay. Can I ask you something else, if you could help with this. At the time you were down there, the time that you're saying is 9 o'clock or just after, around that time, do you recall one of the doctors being present, a gentleman, David Harkness?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I don't.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Right. I don't want you to be at any disadvantage with this. When you say you don't, do you mean you don't and he wasn't there or you don't and he might be there but you just cannot remember that detail?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I didn't see anybody else on that occasion when I went down to the unit.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I understand what you have said. Let me just ask a little more detail about that, whether this helps. Do you recall a conversation where you were there with Ms Letby and a male doctor and talking about some medication that would be given to [Baby E]? This is before you went down at the time of resuscitation. This is the earlier one. Do you recall that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No. The only person in that room was Lucy Letby. There was only me and her there.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: And that's the only person you say you saw?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: That's the only person I had a conversation with.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So if I'm suggesting there was a doctor who was around at that time, that's something you actually disagree with?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I disagree with that.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's why I wanted to be clear. I didn't want to leave it that you might be saying that you couldn't remember in fairness to you, [Mother of Babies E & F].
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Okay. I disagree.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: All right. I'm suggesting there was --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Okay.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: -- on behalf of Ms Letby.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It was a conversation in which you were involved and Lucy Letby and Dr Harkness. That's what is being suggested about some medication for [Baby E].
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I disagree with that.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I wanted to be quite clear about that.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Well, exactly. You're saying you can't remember anything like that happening, it didn't happen?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: No, I was actually told that the registrar would be down and she had made that call.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: But at no time do you say the registrar did actually put in an appearance at that point?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Not at all.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: So we disagree about that bit?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I disagree, yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Moving forwards now, and in fact after what happened at 11 o'clock, you went downstairs, didn't you, at the time that they were trying to give help to [Baby E] when he was very ill; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I'm not going to ask you any details at all but can I just ask you this, [Mother of Babies E & F]: could you see what was happening in the room at that time?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I could see people stood around the incubator. I could see through a window.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: And could you see blood then, do you mind me asking?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: There was people stood round him, I couldn't see anything.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Are you aware, you may not be, but I'll just ask, that they have a set procedure on that unit for how nurses are meant to help families when a bereavement has taken place. Are you aware of that now?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I don't know about that specific hospital, but I do know that other hospitals do have procedures in place.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: All right. Are you aware now that sometimes they have procedures like taking handprints or footprints and making memory boxes? Is that something you know now?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I know now, yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: And Ms Letby took care of [Baby E] after he died, didn't she?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: And you have described some of the things that she did.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: And she was the nurse who had been with [Baby E] beforehand, as far as you understand, is that correct, [Mother of Babies E & F]?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: (Witness nods).
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We've nearly finished, just one final area. It's always helpful just to pause. This is something different, this is about what you told us about the post-mortem, the discussion about the post-mortem.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So the jury can follow who it was with, because you talked about "she". There was a female doctor, wasn't there, who you had the discussion with?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: In fact we're going to find the doctor's name is [Dr C]. You may or may not remember.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Not at all.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: But that's the doctor. When you and your husband eventually decided that you wouldn't have a post-mortem, was that largely because she had explained in a way why there was little point in having a post-mortem?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So in a way, she had directed you in that decision, hadn't she, swayed you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: I felt so, yes.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: All right. [Mother of Babies E & F], thank you for answering my questions.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Re-examination by MR JOHNSON
Just two clarification issues, [Mother of Babies E & F], okay?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: You described the blood that you saw on [Baby E]'s -- around [Baby E]'s mouth as being "not completely fresh", I think were your words. What was it about its appearance that drove you to that conclusion?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: It was stained and it was... (Pause). It wasn't dripping, it was smudged. It's really hard to explain, isn't it? It didn't look completely dry, but it didn't look like it was...
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Was there anything about the colour that --
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: It was darker.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Darker?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: It wasn't... Yeah.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I think most people know that very fresh blood is the colour of his Lordship's gown.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes. It wasn't like that.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Dark blood is a much darker colour. Where was it on the spectrum as you remember?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Um... Darker, but it was... Like I said, it wasn't...
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: It's really hard to explain. It was darker, it wasn't bright red, it was... Yeah, it was darker than that.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't know how else to explain it.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: No, no, it's all right.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: It was all there (indicating).
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: For the benefit of the record, you're again indicating below the bottom lip to the top of the chin area.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: As part of the questioning about the timing of the phone call, it was suggested to you that there had been an incident over timing. Do you remember?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: What was the incident over timing?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: The incident over timing was a report had come from the Countess of Chester and the time difference was very -- it seemed to be out by an hour of my recollection of things. My recollection of things -- I know what time it was and in that moment I thought I know that I literally had come back upstairs because I didn't take my phone with me and I spoke to my husband. I know that I did that. That's when I contacted the telephone company to get things right in my mind as well because I knew and I couldn't understand why the hospital would be so far out with that.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: So what, it was being suggested to you that something had happened an hour later than you remembered it happening?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: Yes, and I knew that that wasn't the case.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: By reference to the telephone call?
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: MOTHER E&F: But I knew it in my mind and then I got some evidence for myself.
blocks.speaker: JOHNSON

blocks.text: Okay. Does your Lordship have any questions?
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: I don't. Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: That completes your evidence. You're free to go.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We're going to have our break now and the next witness is your husband.
